the Ln form covalent bonds with SWNTs in the solid phase, but the degree of ionic character increases with increasing Ln ionic radius.
Ln metal complexation with SWNTs is covalent in nature.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lanthanides, which have a wide range of oxidation states, are capable of forming both ionic and co-valent bonds with SWNTs, and that the bonding is determined by both the nature of the metal and the electronic structure of the SWNTs.
the conductivity behavior of Ln-SWNTs can be explained by the formation of co-hapto bonds, which is consistent with the ionic character of the Ln-SWNT bond.
the conductivity of SWNTs is enhanced when they interact with electropositive metals and this enhancement is due to the formation of bis-hexahapo bonds between the metal and the SWNTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to tune the electronic structure and properties of SC SWNTs by using a small amount of the metal dopant.
the conductivity behavior of Ln metal complexes on SWNTs is not a simple function of the metal's ionic radius or its position in the periodic table.
the lanthanides can be used to tune the electronic structure of semiconductors, and that this can be done with a precision not possible with the more electroposive alkali metals.
